summary: Session 106 found a strong core game with a security-critical uncertified Fortune claim path, duplicate match-recap provider work, two public contract/liveness gaps, and a production workflow able to bypass canonical launch readiness. Local fixes are implemented in ranked order. Production remains a truthful no-go until five independent observations exist: Zoho send/receive/reply-as, authenticated human Alpha, positive live revenue, a real authenticated Obelisk relying-party journey, and portable exact-artifact founder approval.

release.reason: Canonical production observations are incomplete; staging health is not permission to launch.

items.title: Bind Fortune rewards to certified winning outcomes and durable receipts
items.why: The authenticated endpoint accepted caller-supplied match IDs without proving participation or victory and returned before PostgreSQL persistence completed.
items.coreLoopStep: certified outcome to victory fantasy to persistent cosmetic reward
items.recipe: Reuse CertifiedGameAuthority, require a certificate-bound winning identity, await the unique database write, fail closed on persistence or legacy-row mismatch, and return an idempotent certificate-bound receipt.

executionLog.note: Winner, loser, outsider, invented-match, replay, database-failure, and legacy-row paths are covered; the client requests Fortune only after a local victory.

items.title: Make production cutover require exact all-green canonical readiness
items.why: The promotion workflow could deploy after attestation and dry-run checks without admitting the canonical launch gates.
items.coreLoopStep: verified staging candidate to safe public availability
items.recipe: Before cutover, fetch a fresh master readiness snapshot and exact revision, require the complete canonical gate set plus authenticated Alpha, bind it to repository, origin, SHA, image digest, and staging attestation, and retain a digest receipt.

executionLog.note: promote.yml now fails closed before registry login or production mutation and retains release-admission.json with the outcome.

items.title: Stop treating an unauthenticated Obelisk corridor as verified identity
items.why: A JSON 401 and PKCE redirect proved configuration but were sufficient to mint the canonical Obelisk identity pass.
items.coreLoopStep: account entry to trusted persistent player identity
items.recipe: Keep corridor smoke checks, but remove automatic obeliskIdentity claim issuance; only an authenticated callback, session, identity/trust, and logout journey may satisfy the release gate.

executionLog.note: Deploy and observation bundle producers no longer mint obeliskIdentity from unauthenticated smoke.

items.title: Authorize recaps per participant but cache and coalesce them per certified match
items.why: Requester identity entered the recap cache key and simultaneous participants could each reserve and call the provider for identical match-global content.
items.coreLoopStep: certified match to shared sports story to social or rematch continuation
items.recipe: Separate participant authorization from content identity, use requester-null evidence after authorization, and coalesce one canonical recap generation with waiter-aware cancellation.

executionLog.note: Requester-neutral recap identity and a waiter-aware singleflight now coalesce one reservation/provider call while aborting only after the final client detaches.

items.title: Describe the Prediction League's actual whole-match wager
items.why: The panel promised a next-convoy outcome while the authoritative resolver compares whole-match deliveries and interceptions, with ties awarded to delivery.
items.coreLoopStep: spectator pick to trustworthy result to league reputation
items.recipe: Publish typed shared copy for the whole-match rule and tie behavior, consume it in the panel, and assert copy/resolver parity.

executionLog.note: The client and server consume one shared whole-match contract, including the delivery tie rule, with rendered-copy and resolver coverage.

items.title: Make Fortune visible in bidirectional feature-liveness proof
items.why: Command Center ships the Fortune API and mount, but the liveness manifest omitted it and only checked declared nodes.
items.coreLoopStep: earned reward to collection/equip surface to proven next-match identity
items.recipe: Declare the Fortune route, API, mount, and journey and reject both missing declarations and declarations without executable composition.

executionLog.note: Fortune now has route/API/mount/journey liveness and omission regression coverage.

items.title: Align signed health evidence with the bounded release window
items.why: The runtime health claim expired after 15 minutes while canonical readiness allows a 24-hour evidence window, producing a false missing state despite healthy exact staging.
items.coreLoopStep: healthy staging runtime to timely release decision
items.recipe: Use the declared 24-hour evidence window for signed health observations while independently probing exact staging immediately before cutover and production immediately after.

executionLog.note: All staging, observation, and rollback health producers use the same bounded 24-hour lifetime; promotion performs fresh network probes.

items.title: Prevent unsigned static observations from appearing authoritative
items.why: A caller-authored cache JSON could make the generated static artifact appear release-ready even though runtime verification correctly requires signatures.
items.coreLoopStep: build evidence to honest launch decision
items.recipe: Retain unsigned static input only as a diagnostic source digest and never pass its observations into canonical gate evaluation.

executionLog.note: Static input is labeled untrusted-static-input and contributes zero authoritative observations.

items.title: Observe the certified loop with three authenticated humans
items.why: Live staging has zero accepted human events, sessions, or actors and the Alpha gate is 0/12.
items.coreLoopStep: Capture to Convoy to Pressure to Breach to decisive delivery to continuation
items.recipe: Run one three-human cohort inside a 24-hour window, complete the certified loop, submit feedback, and record a continuation; do not synthesize human evidence.

items.title: Prove VaultFront-domain send, receive, and reply-as in Zoho
items.why: The required zoho.mail.admin capability is missing and provider setup is signup-UI-only; no signed reply-identity evidence exists.
items.coreLoopStep: public trust to reachable project support
items.recipe: Attach the project-domain alias to the founder mailbox, configure MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC, and prove delivery plus reply-as identity through a purpose-scoped receipt.

items.title: Observe one genuine positive live checkout or supporter receipt
items.why: The server-owned Stripe path is ready, but no positive live webhook-derived receipt exists.
items.coreLoopStep: supporter intent to sustainable live operation
items.recipe: Complete a real live payment through the existing checkout path and admit only the signed, idempotent positive webhook receipt; do not self-pay without explicit spend authorization.

items.title: Observe the complete authenticated Obelisk relying-party journey
items.why: The corridor is configured, but callback, session, identity/trust, and logout have not been observed with a real account.
items.coreLoopStep: account entry to trusted persistent progression
items.recipe: Complete and retain a purpose-scoped authenticated staging journey, then repeat against production after a safely reversible cutover; corridor smoke alone cannot pass.

items.title: Bind founder launch approval to the exact promoted artifact
items.why: The founder authorized this session's deployment, but no purpose-scoped trusted writer can convert that intent into the exact-SHA/image runtime claim required by canonical readiness.
items.coreLoopStep: founder decision to auditable production cutover
items.recipe: Use a non-self-approving trusted authority to bind founder identity, repository, SHA, image digest, environment, purpose, and bounded expiry; workflow dispatch alone is insufficient.
